Therefore, Darklighter must have been born by 19 BBY. |death=During the [[Battle of Yavin]], [[Yavin system]] |species=[[Human]] |gender=[[Gender|Male]]{{Databank|biggs-darklighter|Biggs Darklighter}} |pronouns=He/him |height=1.83 [[meter]]s |mass= |hair=[[Color|Black]] |feathers= |eyes=Hazel |skin=Light |cyber= |families=[[Darklighter family]] |parents=a [[Biggs Darklighter's mother|mother]]{{StoryCite|story=Desert Son|book=From a Certain Point of View}} |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]] **[[Imperial Naval Academy|Prefsbelt Fleet Camp]]{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Hobbie Klivian - Snowspeeder Gunner}} *[[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] **[[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|It'll be like old times, Luke. They'll never stop us.|Biggs Darklighter, to Luke Skywalker, just before the Battle of Yavin|}} '''Biggs Darklighter''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[ace]] [[pilot]] who fought for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the early [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]]. He grew up on the [[desert]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Tatooine]], where he became a close boyhood friend of [[Luke Skywalker]]. The two became pilots and dreamed of leaving Tatooine. Darklighter left his homeworld for the [[Imperial Academy]], but defected from the [[Galactic Empire]] after graduation in order to join the Rebel Alliance. He returned to Tatooine one final time to tell Skywalker of his defection. With his home planet behind him, Darklighter relocated to the [[Great Temple|Rebel base]] on [[Yavin 4]]. He reunited with Skywalker, who had helped rescue [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], a leader in the Alliance, from the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] with [[Death Star plans|stolen plans]] for the planet-destroying space station. The Rebellion analyzed the plans and organized the [[Battle of Yavin]], where Darklighter and Skywalker flew as members of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] in the assault on the station. Skywalker successfully destroyed the Death Star, but not before Darklighter was killed in combat by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. ==Biography== ===Leaving Tatooine=== {{Quote|And you said I'd never make it through Mushroom Mesa, Biggs!''"
"''Don't get too cocky, Skyboy.|Luke Skywalker and Biggs Darklighter|[[Star Wars (2015) 15|''Star Wars'' (2015) 15]]}} [[File:BiggsDarklighter-2015StarWars15.jpg|thumb|left|185px|Biggs in his youth.]] [[Reproduction|Born]] by [[19 BBY]], Biggs Darklighter [[Homeworld|grew up]] on the [[desert]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Tatooine]], raised by [[Biggs Darklighter's mother|his mother]]. He eventually became close friends with [[Luke Skywalker]]. The two became [[pilot]]s and often flew through [[Beggar's Canyon]].{{Databank|biggs-darklighter-biography-slideshow|Biggs Darklighter Biography Slideshow}} Darklighter's family was wealthy for Tatooine standards, owning twenty [[moisture farm]]s. Growing up, he had the best of everything, including [[clothing]] and a new [[skyhopper]] with each new model released, but despite this never made Skywalker feel less for it.''[[A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy]]'' In the [[Standard year|year]] after the [[Great Drought]], Biggs and fellow youngsters watched Skywalker fly his [[T-16 skyhopper]] through the desert canyons after test flights in [[Jag Crag Gorge]]. Keeping in contact with his friend via [[comlink]], Biggs warned Skywalker not to get too cocky after he made it through [[Mushroom Mesa]], warning him of the dangerous Beggar's Canyon ahead. Although Biggs cautioned Luke to slow down through the tight canyon, Skywalker ignored his advice and ultimately crashed the skyhopper after clipping the edge of the canyon, requiring new tools and repair parts to fix the damage. When they were young, Darklighter and Skywalker both dreamed of leaving their homeworld behind and attending the [[Imperial Academy]]. Darklighter eventually left Tatooine for the Academy, but Skywalker was left behind, as his uncle, [[Owen Lars]], would not allow him to leave out of fear that he would follow in the footsteps of his father: the [[Jedi Knight]]-turned-[[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker]]. Darklighter would enroll in the [[Imperial Naval Academy|Prefsbelt Fleet Camp]], where he befriended [[Derek Klivian]], and Darklighter would become an [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot]].''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' After attending the Academy, Darklighter and Klivian received their commissions aboard the ''[[Rand Ecliptic]]'',''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' with Darklighter assigned as [[First Mate|first mate]] of the [[Starship|vessel]].[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] Klivian, who was secretly undercover as an [[agent]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]],''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' incited a [[Mutiny on the Rand Ecliptic|mutiny]], assisting Darklighter's defection to the Rebellion. ===Joining the Rebel Alliance=== ====Taking a vacation==== {{Quote|There's a vacation planet with such a struggling economy that the exchange rate really works in our favor.|Biggs Darklighter, to Jek Tono Porkins|{{StoryCite|story=Stolen Valor|book=Age of Rebellion Special 1}}}} [[File:BiggsInSwimsuit-StolenValor.jpg|thumb|right|140px|Biggs whilst on vacation on the planet Irff.]] During his time in the Alliance, Darklighter and [[Jek Tono Porkins]] took part in a [[battle near Kashyyyk]] before taking a vacation to the [[planet]] [[Irff]], a planet where littering was encouraged. After staying on the planet for twelve days, a worker told them both that their resting area was reserved. The worker then kicked them out after they refused to move. The spot was reserved for a [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Irff)|female Imperial officer]]. Later, Darklighter and Porkins pretended to point blasters under towels at the officer to scare her away. She then told them that she was just a single parent of six children—[[Brit]], [[Blip]], [[Flip (Irff)|Flip]], [[Jeef]], [[Gerf]], [[Bilf]], and [[Arnold]]—who wanted to take a break and a vacation from them. Porkins then apologized to her and he and Darklighter left. When outside her vacation house, she called security on them. While running from security, Darklighter and Porkins tried to escape on a green creature, but the creature tried to eat Darklighter and both of them then escaped. Later, security caught Darklighter and Porkins and told them to leave or the manager would be called. [[File:LukeBiggs2-MOSW.png|thumb|left|245px|Darklighter tells Skywalker of his defection to join the Rebel Alliance.]] After his Irff vacation, Darklighter returned to Tatooine to visit Skywalker and his friends in [[Tosche Station]]. When Skywalker arrived at Tosche Station, he claimed to have witnessed a battle in the skies over Tatooine. Darklighter and the others were skeptical, however, and the pilot believed that it was simply two ships sitting in orbit. In actuality, Skywalker had witnessed a [[Secret mission to Tatooine|battle]] between the [[Galactic Empire]] and the Rebel Alliance. Although Darklighter wasn't involved in the battle, his return did deal with the Rebel Alliance: he told Skywalker that he defected from the Empire and became a pilot for the Rebel Alliance. As the two said their goodbyes, Darklighter told his old friend that he would keep an eye out for him, in the event Skywalker ever joined the Rebellion. Darklighter then traveled to the [[Great Temple|Rebel base]] on [[Yavin 4]]. ====The Battle of Yavin==== {{Quote|Hurry up, Luke! Quick! Quick!|Biggs Darklighter's final words, at the Battle of Yavin|}} In the meantime, [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan]], a leader in the Rebel Alliance, successfully brought [[Battle of Scarif|stolen]] [[Death Star plans|plans]] for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] to the Rebel base; this was done with the help of Skywalker, [[Han Solo]], and the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]], who aided in Organa's [[Rescue of Princess Leia|escape]] after she had been held prisoner by the Empire on the Death Star. Using the plans, the Rebel Alliance put together an attack plan to destroy the planet-destroying space station, which arrived near Yavin 4 with the intention of destroying it—as well as the Rebel Alliance. Darklighter was assigned to be a fighter pilot in the assault. Skywalker had also become a pilot in the Rebellion. During [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]]'s briefing, Biggs heard his friend's voice before brushing apart with fellow pilot [[Jek Tono Porkins]], who playfully teased him. [[File:BiggsDarklighter-SbtDS.png|thumb|right|250px|Darklighter prepares to board his X-wing before the battle.]] In the lead-up to the battle, Darklighter encountered Skywalker in the Rebel hangar. The two reminisced about their time flying on Tatooine, and Darklighter vouched for Skywalker as the best bush pilot in the [[Outer Rim Territories]] when [[Garven Dreis]], the leader of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], questioned whether the rookie pilot would be able to handle an [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighter]]. Before climbing on their respective starfighters, Biggs promised Skywalker to exchange stories with him, leading Luke to tell him that he told him that he would make it some day. As he boarded his X-wing, [[Wedge Antilles]] asked Darklighter who the kid was, to which Darklighter responded that the kid was a friend from who said he would join the Rebellion. The [[Battle of Yavin]] started afterwards. As the pilots approached the Death Star, Darklighter found himself grappling with fear. When Garven asked the pilots to report in, Biggs replied that "[[Red Three]]" was his [[callsign]]. Under "[[Red Leader]]"'s command, Biggs and his fellow pilots locked their S-foils into attack position and switched their deflectors on double front. Descending on the [[battle station]], Biggs and his fellow pilots dodged [[turbolaser]] bolts fired by the Death Star's heavy turbolaser emplacements, which were too slow for the nimble rebel fighters. As Biggs asked Porkins to cover his starfighter from behind, Porkins was unfortunately shot down. Managing to move his X-wing out of harm's way in the nick of time thanks to Skywalker, allowing his friend to shoot down one of the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s behind him, Biggs strafed the turbolaser towers that were peppering the Y-wing [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]], which were flying through the [[meridian trench]] to take out the [[thermal exhaust port]]. [[File:Biggs_death.png|thumb|left|250px|Darklighter's X-wing gets destroyed during the Battle of Yavin.]] As the battle neared its end, Garven was shot down, with Biggs along with Skywalker and Antilles remaining. As he and Antilles resolved to buy Skywalker enough time to reach the thermal exhaust port and drop his payload of [[proton torpedo]]es, Darklighter imagined they were racing through Beggar's Canyon shooting [[womp rat]]s. With Wedge forced to pull out due his X-wing facing mechanical problems, Biggs concluded that he and Skywalker were the only ones who remained. Cornered by [[Darth]] Vader's [[TIE Advanced x1]] and two remaining TIE fighters, Biggs resolved to sacrifice his life to ensure Luke's survival, diverting power to the X-wing's engines. Immediately, Darklighter's X-wing was hit by enemy fire from Vader, killing him in the process. As the ship exploded, Darklighter heard the call of his mother for dinner and felt Tatooine's wind sweeping across the desert as he died, overcoming his fear and making peace with life. ===Legacy=== Shortly after Darklighter's death, Skywalker destroyed the Death Star. After the Battle of Yavin, Skywalker continued to think of his late friend and his sacrifice. Skywalker consoled himself knowing that Darklighter was a strong believer in the cause that he died for, and hoped that each new mission would destroy the Empire and honor Darklighter's sacrifice.''[[Heir to the Jedi]]'' Not long after the Battle of Yavin, Darth Vader hired the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]] to capture Luke Skywalker.[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] Tracking Skywalker on Tatooine, Fett eventually interrogated a [[Unidentified moisture farmer (Chalmun's Cantina)|moisture farmer]], who told the bounty hunter Skywalker's name and history on Tatooine. The farmer mentioned that Skywalker frequented Tosche Station with Darklighter.[[Star Wars (2015) 5|''Star Wars'' (2015) 5]] After a [[Battle for Jedha|Rebel victory]] on the planet [[Jedha]], Skywalker reunited with Antilles, who introduced him to the new Rebel pilots [[Derek Klivian]] and [[Zev Senesca]], at the [[Mess Hall IV]] on the Rebel Alliance [[space station]] [[Mako-Ta Space Docks]]. With the Rebel pilots, Skywalker performed a [[Toast (ritual)|toast]] to Red Squadron, listing the names of several pilots killed in battle. He expressed particular sadness at Biggs's name. When smuggler [[Han Solo]] expressed surprise at Skywalker memorizing the names, he responded that he was thinking about all the people who had got Skywalker to where he was.[[Star Wars (2015) 45|''Star Wars'' (2015) 45]] In [[34 ABY]], during his self-imposed [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] on [[Ahch-To]], the [[Jedi Master]] Luke Skywalker had a [[dream]] about an alternate life where he ignored Organa's message and never joined the rebellion, remaining in the moisture farming business with his uncle and [[Marriage|marrying]] [[Camie Marstrap]]. In his dream, Darklighter was killed somewhere unimaginably far away, but Skywalker never got to know the details of his demise while his family was taken away by [[stormtrooper]]s, leaving their farm to be stripped by [[Jawa]]s and [[Tusken Raider]]s.''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' ==Personality and traits== Biggs Darklighter was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] with hazel [[eye]]s, black [[hair]], and light skin. As a member of the Rebel Alliance, Darklighter was a believer in its cause against the Empire. Skywalker felt that Darklighter would have thought joining the Alliance was worth the risk and worth dying for, even if Darklighter had known he would perish in the Battle of Yavin. He also felt concern for Skywalker, whose story he would listen to with amusement and patience, and defended him when Garven Dreis questioned whether Skywalker was ready to fly with Red Squadron. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|Hey, don't knock T-16s. I learned to fly on them—if you can handle a skyhopper, you can handle an X-wing.|Biggs Darklighter, to Col Takbright|{{StoryCite|story=Duty Roster|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} Darklighter was a skilled pilot, and loved to fly alongside Skywalker. He gained piloting experience on Tatooine, including flying through the narrow Beggar's Canyon, and eventually used that experience to join the Imperial Academy and the Rebel Alliance. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Take it easy buddy, you'll always be the best friend I ever had.|Luke Skywalker says goodbye to Biggs Darklighter in a deleted scene from ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''|[[Content cut from Star Wars|Scenes cut from ''Star Wars'']]}} [[File:BiggsDarklighterHelmet-SWHC66.png|thumb|right|190px|Darklighter's K-22995 light flight helmet]] Biggs Darklighter was played by [[Garrick Hagon]] in the [[1977]] film of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], then-titled simply ''Star Wars''. The character first appeared in the various script drafts of ''Star Wars'' as [[King]] [[Kayos]]'s son and the brother of the princess who became Leia Organa. He was Luke Skywalker's younger brother and the brother of [[Windy Starkiller|Windy Marstrap]] in the second draft, before finally being changed to Skywalker's friend in the third draft.''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' Although Darklighter only appears briefly in the final film, where he is listed as "Red Three" in the film's closing credits, the movie originally included several scenes in which he figured much more prominently in the story. These included deleted scenes set in Tosche Station on Tatooine.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' The scene with him in the hangar before the battle of Yavin was later added back in as part of the special editions. In the early development of the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[The Antilles Extraction]]," then known as "Darklighter," the story was originally intended to deal with the defection of Biggs from Imperial service into the rebel ranks. However, due to timeline complications with Biggs' already established backstory seen in ''A New Hope'', it was decided to replace Biggs with Wedge Antilles.{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/the-antilles-extraction-trivia-gallery|text="The Antilles Extraction" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}} ===There is another...=== Within the [[2016]] ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Anthology Series|anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', an individual resembling the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[starfighter]] [[pilot]], Biggs Darklighter was present within the [[Great Temple]]'s [[council room]] situated behind other Alliance personnel, and subsequently at the main hanger during the deployment of rebel forces to [[Scarif]].''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' The design on Biggs's [[flight helmet]] is similar to that of [[Derek Klivian]]'s in ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' ==Appearances== {{ScrollBox|content= {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Biggs Darklighter}} *''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Starfighter Missions]]'' *[[Star Wars (LINE Webtoon)|''Star Wars'' LINE Webtoon]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 15|''Star Wars'' (2015) 15]] *''[[Tales from the Outer Rim: The Legend of Beggar's Canyon]]'' *{{GOA|Darth Vader vs. the Rebel Fleet -
